clue.text: Footwear on black market?

parts.note: a boot is an item of footwear
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so on can stand for leg

explanation.surface: A question about shoes being sold illegally.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field, so 'on' gives LEG. The question mark flags the adjectival use of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit, smuggled goods, typically spirits or recordings, are what a black market trades in.

clue.text: Escaper does it to strike pose

parts.note: to beat is to strike
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A runaway stops to strike a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: An escaper runs off; the slang phrase means clear off quickly.

clue.text: Bygone period about which monarch appears too keen

parts.note: something over is finished, bygone

indicators.note: about means the monarch's letters go around the word for period

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the monarch
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: In an old era a king or queen comes across as overly enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'which' and 'appears' only knit the surface together. ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively eager and enthusiastic, more than is wise.

clue.text: Smallest article breaks in case

indicators.note: breaks means the article cuts into the word for in case

parts.note: lest means for fear that, in case
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The tiniest item has broken inside its container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' puts A inside LEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, the minimum in size.

clue.text: What snooker player does when past his best?

definitions.text: What snooker player does when past his best?

parts.words: What snooker player does when past his best?
parts.note: a snooker player aims to sink balls into pockets, and someone in decline is said to deteriorate badly

explanation.surface: A question about a washed-up snooker professional.
explanation.walkthrough: To pot is to sink a ball in snooker; the idiom means to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deteriorate, while a snooker player literally attempts a pot.

clue.text: Becomes tearful, as long-haul driver often does

definitions.meaning: eyes brimming with tears are said to well up with water
a lorry driver on a long trip regularly tops the tank with fuel

explanation.surface: A trucker gets emotional on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Two idiomatic senses: eyes brimming with tears, and topping a fuel tank to the brim.

clue.text: Tips of feather spanning bird's bone

indicators.note: spanning means the outer letters stretch around the bird
tips are the two ends of the word feather

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless bird; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: Feather tips stretch over a bird's bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanning' puts F and R around EMU.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh bone, the longest in the human body.

clue.text: Business magnate upset rural gods

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A tycoon has angered the country deities.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Sugar is a British entrepreneur, made a peer, known from the UK version of The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Sugar founded the electronics firm Amstrad and is a famous British tycoon.

clue.text: Co-ordinated discharge of colossal volume

indicators.note: of signals the answer is taken out of the words colossal volume

explanation.surface: A synchronised release of a huge amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A simultaneous firing of several guns is a volley.

clue.text: Remedial treatment from clergy, as purist goes off the rails …

indicators.note: going off the rails means going wild, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A clergyman needs corrective help after a purist goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off the rails' rearranges the fourteen letters of CLERGY AS PURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Operations to repair or reshape the body are a corrective medical treatment.

clue.text: Artistes will have performed here a long time back

indicators.note: back tells us to read the phrase for a long time from its end to its start

parts.note: an era is a long period of history

explanation.surface: Performers played at this venue long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of 'a long time back' (long ago), but it signals the reversal of AN ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stadium or hall where concerts and shows are staged is a venue for performers.

clue.text: Hugo's character originally set in stone, with a touch of arrogance

indicators.note: in places the first letter of set within the gemstone

parts.note: an emerald is a precious stone

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the word set
a touch of means just a little, the first letter of arrogance

explanation.surface: A Victor Hugo heroine described as set in stone and slightly haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside EMERALD, giving ESMERALD, and A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The gypsy dancer in Victor Hugo's novel The Hunchback of Notre-Dame bears this name.

clue.text: Flighty carrot-top pests that'll draw the crowds

indicators.note: flighty means unstable and capricious, so the letters of the following words fly about into a new order

explanation.surface: Capricious red-haired nuisances who attract onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' scrambles the fourteen letters of CARROT, TOP and PESTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A game such as football that is popular to watch draws large audiences of onlookers.

clue.text: See 11
Put a name to American river, longest in country

parts.note: to tag something is to label it with a name
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: Identify the river that is the longest in a certain American country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'country' is not American: the river flows through Spain and Portugal, longest of the Iberian peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterway runs from Spain to Lisbon and is the longest on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: … when involved in ground-breaking match

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside the word for ground-breaking

parts.note: seminal work is highly original and influential
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains, I stay in'

explanation.surface: Continuing from 8 Down, the purist runs amok during a pioneering game.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only carries the story on from 8 Down; this clue's wordplay stands alone. 'involved in' is the container signal, and 'when' standing for IF is a common substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A game in a knockout competition deciding who reaches the final.

clue.text: Picky journalist keen to appear in film

indicators.note: to appear in means to be placed inside, here inside the word for a film

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, a journalist
agog means eagerly excited

explanation.surface: A fussy reporter is eager to star in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to appear in' is the container signal. 'Picky' looks like it belongs to the journalist but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a schoolmaster, fussy and over-precise about small rules and details.

clue.text: Costing the earth? Far from it

definitions.text: Costing the earth? Far from it

parts.words: Costing the earth? Far from it
parts.note: dirt is another word for earth, so the price is soil, which is next to nothing

explanation.surface: Something said to be extremely expensive, then contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Costing the earth means very expensive; read literally, costing earth (dirt) means nearly free.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means extremely inexpensive, the opposite of costing a fortune.

clue.text: Hamlet's best friend?

parts.note: Hamlet was a prince of Denmark, a fine native, and a dog is called man's best friend

explanation.surface: Asks who was closest to Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio seems the answer; but Hamlet himself was a great Dane, and a dog is man's best friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is man's best friend, and this giant breed shares its name with an eminent Dane.

clue.text: Meteor crashes on line — it'll take the pressure

indicators.note: on means the scrambled letters come after the word for line

parts.note: a bar is a line or stripe

indicators.note: crashes suggests the letters smash and reassemble in new order

explanation.surface: A meteor comes down onto a line, taking the impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' is the anagram signal and 'on' places the scrambled letters after the line; 'take the pressure' means measure it, not endure it.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure, so it takes readings of it.

clue.text: Primates show disapproval of entering bars

indicators.note: entering means the jeer goes inside the word for bars

parts.note: to bar is to ban
to boo is to jeer disapprovingly

explanation.surface: Monkeys jeer at being let into pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like pubs but is the verb meaning prohibits; 'entering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Large African and Arabian monkeys, members of the primate order.

clue.text: Flyers grounded during downpour, he assumed

indicators.note: during means the letters run within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Planes are kept on the ground during a storm, someone supposes.
explanation.definitionFit: These large South American birds have wings but cannot fly, so they stay on the ground.

clue.text: See 8
Picture barrister in Parisian bar

parts.note: brief is British slang for a lawyer, especially a barrister
en is French for in
a counter is the bar where drinks are served

explanation.surface: A lawyer pictured in a Paris bar.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEF is everyday British slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a film, and this 1945 David Lean film is a classic of British cinema.

clue.text: Democracy one's not found in island nation

indicators.note: not found in means these letters are removed from the island nation

parts.note: Indonesia is an archipelago nation
one's gives the letters of ones

explanation.surface: A country of islands supposedly without democracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not found in' removes ONES from INDONESIA.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Asian country is often called the world's largest democracy.

clue.text: See 21
German, who drew back when cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letters round to the end of the word for back

parts.note: the stern is the back of a boat

explanation.surface: A German man withdrew while on a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drew' means painted, not retreated: 'cycling' moves ST of STERN to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German Surrealist painter and artist.

clue.text: Inadequate squad with invading force

indicators.note: invading means the letter for force pushes into the word for squad

parts.note: a unit is a squad of soldiers
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A weak team is being overrun by an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' puts F inside UNIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Not suitable or not competent enough for a purpose.

clue.text: Priest in training ultimately ignored church law

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter, which is ignored, dropped

parts.note: an ordinand is a candidate studying for holy orders
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A trainee priest overlooked an ecclesiastical rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately ignored' drops the last letter of ORDINAND; CE is then added.
explanation.definitionFit: An authoritative decree or rule, here one laid down by a church.

clue.text: Large quantity of water taken by female shaving

indicators.note: taken by means the word for water is attached to the abbreviation for female

parts.note: a lake is a large body of water

explanation.surface: A woman uses plenty of water while shaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin sliver pared off something, such as a chip of wood or chocolate.

clue.text: Brightly coloured small mini-vehicle?

parts.note: a car with the diminutive ending -let, as in piglet, makes a jokey little car

explanation.surface: A query about a vivid little car.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLET is invented for the joke, hence the question mark: -let makes things small.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid bright red is a brilliant shade.

clue.text: Present judge and jury finally go off

parts.note: to put a case or question is to present it
a ref, referee, judges a game

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of jury

explanation.surface: Present the judge and jury, then finally leave the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that rots or decays is said to go bad.
